scenarios.title: The Group Text
scenarios.text: The specialists have a group text, and you're not in it yet.

choices.label: Ask to be added
choices.result: You ask the punter to add you. You're in by lunch, and the first message is a meme about you.

choices.label: Earn your way in
choices.result: You don't ask. After a good week of practice, you're added without a word.

choices.label: Don't care
choices.result: You decide you don't need a group text. It's quieter. You miss the inside jokes.

scenarios.title: The Ride to Practice
scenarios.text: You don't have a car yet, and the veteran who offered rides keeps forgetting.

choices.label: Ride with another rookie
choices.result: You ride with another rookie every day. The drives turn into the best part of the week.

choices.label: Take a car service
choices.result: You take a car service and read on the way. It's expensive, and relaxing.

choices.label: Bike to practice
choices.result: You bike to practice every morning. Your legs are tired, and strong.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Show
scenarios.text: The rookies have to put on a talent show for the veterans, and you have no talent besides kicking.

choices.label: Commit to something ridiculous
choices.result: You do a dramatic poetry reading about the long snapper. The room cries laughing.

choices.label: Organize the whole show
choices.result: You organize the rookies' acts and run the show like a coach. It's the best one in years.

choices.label: Do the minimum
choices.result: You do a card trick and sit down. Nobody remembers it.

scenarios.title: The Fan Event
scenarios.text: A season-ticket holders' event, and everyone wants a picture with the new kicker.

choices.label: Take every picture
choices.result: You take every picture and learn a dozen names. Two of them sit behind the bench for years after.

choices.label: Bring the specialists
choices.result: You bring the punter and snapper along. The fans love the 'kicking unit' photo.

choices.label: Leave on time
choices.result: You stay your hour and leave on time. It's fine.

scenarios.title: The Hometown Paper
scenarios.text: Your hometown paper runs a story about you with a photo from your senior prom.

choices.label: Send them a better photo
choices.result: You call the paper, laugh and send a better photo. They run both.

choices.label: Let it be
choices.result: You let it be. The prom photo is now on your locker, courtesy of the veterans.

choices.label: Thank the reporter
choices.result: You call the reporter who wrote it and thank them. They become the first person to tell your story right.

scenarios.title: The Card Signing
scenarios.text: A trading card company wants your signature on a thousand cards in one afternoon.

choices.label: Sign them all
choices.result: You sign a thousand cards in four hours. Your hand hurts, and the check is nice.

choices.label: Sign a few for charity
choices.result: You sign two hundred and donate a set to a children's hospital raffle.

choices.label: Pass
choices.result: You pass. Your hand is grateful.

scenarios.title: The Holder Who Won't Talk
scenarios.text: Your new holder is all business and doesn't talk to rookies.

choices.label: Learn the routine silently
choices.result: You learn the holder's routine by watching. By week three, you're in sync without a word.

choices.label: Win the holder over
choices.result: You bring the holder lunch and ask about their family. It takes a month, and then it's easy.

choices.label: Out-prepare them
choices.result: You show up early every day until the holder starts showing up earlier.

scenarios.title: The First Night Game
scenarios.text: The first night game under the lights, and you can't sleep the night before.

choices.label: Do nothing all day
choices.result: You read, nap and do nothing all day. You're calm by kickoff.

choices.label: Talk to the sports psychologist
choices.result: You call the team's sports psychologist. Two exercises, and you sleep like a baby.

choices.label: Call home
choices.result: You call {parent}, who tells you about every night game he ever watched you in. You laugh yourself to sleep.

scenarios.title: Sleeping on the Plane
scenarios.text: The team plane at midnight, and you can't sleep on planes.

choices.label: Bring a sleep kit
choices.result: You bring an eye mask, earplugs and a pillow. The veterans mock you; you sleep four hours.

choices.label: Join the card game
choices.result: You join the card game in the back. You lose a few dollars and make three friends.

choices.label: Watch film
choices.result: You watch film on your tablet the whole flight. You land exhausted and very prepared.

scenarios.title: The Hotel Roommate
scenarios.text: Your road roommate snores, sleepwalks and talks about his ex all night.

choices.label: Listen to him
choices.result: You listen. He's going through a lot, and you become his person on road trips.

choices.label: Ask for a new roommate
choices.result: You ask the travel staff for a new roommate. You sleep, and he's a little hurt.

choices.label: Bring earplugs and set rules
choices.result: You bring earplugs and set a lights-out time. It mostly works.

scenarios.title: The Waiver Wire
scenarios.text: A rookie from your class is cut and claimed by another club within an hour.

choices.label: Text him
choices.result: You text him congratulations on the new club. He calls you every Sunday that season.

choices.label: Take the lesson
choices.result: You treat it as a lesson about how fast this league moves, and kick extra that afternoon.

choices.label: Feel it and move on
choices.result: You let yourself feel it for an evening. Then you go to sleep.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Contract
scenarios.text: You finally read your rookie contract all the way through.

choices.label: Read every clause
choices.result: You read every clause and call your agent with six questions. You learn what a guarantee really means.

choices.label: Focus on the incentives
choices.result: You focus on the incentive clauses and tape them inside your locker.

choices.label: Skim it
choices.result: You skim it and trust your agent. It's fine.

scenarios.title: The Kicker Down the Hall
scenarios.text: The punter is your age and acts like he's been here twenty years.

choices.label: Become friends anyway
choices.result: You become friends anyway. It turns out he's as nervous as you are.

choices.label: Compete with him
choices.result: You turn every specialist drill into a quiet competition with him. You both get better.

choices.label: Ignore him
choices.result: You ignore him. The specialists' room is awkward all season.
